title: Frühstück, Mittagessen, Abendbrot
summary: Germany's three-meal rhythm and the cultural concept of Abendbrot — a cold bread supper instead of a second hot meal

blocks.title: Drei Mahlzeiten, ein Tag
blocks.body: The German day runs on three meals: **Frühstück** (breakfast), **Mittagessen** (lunch, traditionally the main meal), and **Abendbrot** — literally "evening bread". Instead of cooking a second hot meal, many Germans eat *Brot* with cold cuts, cheese, and pickles for dinner. It's not laziness — it's a whole culture built around good bread.
blocks.callout: *Abendbrot* is the word AND the meal — a whole culture in one compound noun.

blocks.title: Regionale Namen für Brötchen
blocks.body: *Brötchen* is the standard word everywhere in Germany — but locally, people have pet names for it. In Berlin, Lena calls it *eine Schrippe*; head south and you might hear *Weck*. For speaking and writing, stick with the standard: **Brötchen**.

pairs.left: Mittagessen — warm, oft Kartoffeln oder Reis
pairs.right: Abendbrot — kalt, Brot mit Wurst und Käse
pairs.note: Lunch is traditionally the hot meal; dinner is simple and cold.
